scope.definition: Operational evidence for software projects in which agents or deterministic bots take work from a trigger (issue, alert, dependency update, scheduled audit, chat/ticket) through investigation and a proposed or merged change. Production means used on a live organization's real repositories/workflow, not merely a benchmark.
scope.covered: Issue-to-PR coding agents (Devin, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot cloud agent), internal/customer deployments, human-AI productivity experiments and surveys, and mature dependency-maintenance automation (Renovate/Dependabot) as a lower-risk baseline.
scope.excluded: Pure model leaderboard scores as proof of production reliability; unverified social-media anecdotes; fully autonomous direct-to-production deployment claims without auditable evidence. Benchmarks appear only to explain the production-evidence gap.

current_state.verified: Agents can run real repository work asynchronously in isolated environments, use repository/ticket/observability context, execute builds/tests/linters, and open PRs. Cognition documents 659 agent PRs merged into its own codebase in one week in February 2026. GitHub documents an ephemeral Actions-backed cloud-agent path and explicit human approval controls. Renovate provides mature CI-gated automerge for narrow dependency updates.
current_state.vendor_claims: Rakuten reports a 79% feature time-to-market reduction and a seven-hour autonomous code task; TELUS reports 30% faster code shipping and large aggregate savings; Cognition reports production session measurement across eight deployments. These are useful existence proofs, but are selected vendor/customer accounts without raw denominators, control groups, full costs, or post-merge defect rates.
current_state.independent_reality: Results vary sharply by task, user, and measurement. Answer.AI got only 3 successes in 20 Devin tasks. METR's early-2025 RCT found experienced maintainers 19% slower, while its later 2026 data weakly suggested speedup but was too selection-biased for a reliable estimate. Stack Overflow shows high use but low trust and substantial debugging burden.
current_state.bottom_line: As of 2026-09-13, supervised issue-to-PR operation is demonstrably usable; unattended general software ownership is not. Narrow, testable, reversible maintenance can be highly automated. Product/spec decisions, cross-repository changes, difficult validation, security-sensitive actions and production deployment still need explicit human or policy gates.

representative_systems.evidence_role: Counterweight to selected customer stories and lab benchmarks.
Rare published operational funnels proving that reproduction, overfitting filters and human review dominate apparent patch success.

primary_evidence.claim: Cognition used Devin through web, Slack, Linear/Jira, CLI and API and merged 659 Devin-authored PRs in one week; review became the bottleneck.
primary_evidence.classification: verified first-party report, not independently audited

primary_evidence.claim: Cognition's production estimator dataset had 258 sessions from 126 users across eight deployments; it removes roughly 1-20% of non-PR sessions as unproductive by customer, and admits merged PRs can hide later defects.

GitHub's cloud agent runs in an ephemeral Actions environment, produces a branch/PR, consumes Actions minutes and AI credits, and is limited to one repository/branch/PR with a 59-minute hard session cap.

GitHub keeps Actions workflows behind a write-user's approval by default, limits triggers to write users, requires an extra PR approval where approvals already apply, and identifies prompt injection as a risk.
Rakuten reports 24-to-5-working-day feature delivery and a seven-hour single-run vLLM change; TELUS reports 30% faster engineering delivery.
primary_evidence.classification: vendor/customer claims; no raw study or independent audit

primary_evidence.claim: Renovate waits for required checks and its maintainers advise automerge only for changes a human would merge anyway, with good tests for production dependencies.
primary_evidence.classification: verified workflow guidance, not an outcome study

primary_evidence.claim: Wiz reports that a feature-flagged Python-to-Go migration matched 99% of production outputs, yet the remaining 1% revealed 20-30 distinct issues; testing, differential production comparison and feature flags were required before full rollout.
primary_evidence.classification: vendor/customer report with unusually concrete failure evidence

primary_evidence.claim: Cognition reports a 67% Devin PR merge rate in 2025 versus 34% the prior year, but merge is not issue resolution, defect-free operation or net value.
primary_evidence.classification: vendor aggregate telemetry; denominator/task mix and review cost not disclosed

primary_evidence.claim: GitHub's billing team reports technical-debt work changed from weeks of intermittent attention to minutes writing a precise issue plus hours reviewing/iterating, and warns against 100+-file agent PRs.
primary_evidence.classification: first-party internal case study without standardized baseline

independent_evidence.result: Answer.AI month-long field use: 3 successes, 14 failures and 3 inconclusive among 20 tasks. Impossible tasks could consume more than a day while the agent invented nonexistent capabilities; an attempted feature consumed several human hours before the team wrote it in about 90 minutes.
independent_evidence.strength: Direct detailed practitioner report with task appendix; small, one team, early product version.

independent_evidence.result: METR early-2025 RCT: 16 experienced open-source developers completed 246 real issues in familiar repositories and took 19% longer with AI; PR quality was similar.
independent_evidence.strength: Randomized real-work design; narrow population, tools and 20-minute-to-4-hour task range.

independent_evidence.result: METR 2026 follow-up raw estimates suggested 18% speedup for returning developers and 4% for new recruits, but intervals included no effect and authors judged selection/timing bias severe; 30-50% reported withholding some tasks from randomization.
independent_evidence.strength: Transparent update; explicitly not a reliable causal estimate.

independent_evidence.result: Stack Overflow 2025: 46% distrusted AI accuracy versus 33% who trusted it; 66% encountered almost-right results and 45% said debugging generated code takes more time. For agents, 87% expressed accuracy concern and 81% security/privacy concern.
independent_evidence.strength: Large broad survey; self-report, respondents and question denominators differ.

independent_evidence.result: DORA 2024 observed that 25% higher AI adoption correlated with 7.5% better documentation, 3.4% better code quality and 3.1% faster review, but also 1.5% lower throughput and 7.2% lower stability.
independent_evidence.strength: Broad industry research, but associations are not causal and cover AI assistance generally, not only autonomous agents.

independent_evidence.result: A 2023 peer-reviewed Dependabot study covering 1,823 projects and 502,752 PRs found >70% merged, median four-hour merge lag, and mean technical lag falling from 48.99 to 25.38 days after 90 days. Yet 11.3% of projects deprecated it; notification noise, missing grouping/configuration/package support/automerge were cited, and most switchers chose Renovate.
independent_evidence.strength: Large observational production dataset plus 131-developer survey; correlation/adoption selection and 2023 product behavior limit causal/current inference.

independent_evidence.result: Repairnator's continuous-operation funnel processed 11,523 CI failures, locally reproduced 3,551 (30.82%), generated 15 patches (0.13%), and submitted none because all overfit despite passing the failing test.
independent_evidence.strength: Direct operational funnel shows environment/test-oracle burden; 2017-2018 Java ecosystem is foundational rather than current frontier-agent evidence.

independent_evidence.result: Facebook's SapFix first three months covered 57 crashes: 165 candidates, 131 that built/passed tests, 55 exposed to developers; about half of exposed fixes were judged correct, and all 18 revert suggestions were declined. A high-volume experiment was stopped after three days to avoid reviewer spam.
independent_evidence.strength: Peer-reviewed industrial deployment on six very large apps; narrow crash repair and 2019 technology.

independent_evidence.result: Facebook Getafix surfaced suggestions for about 250 null-dereference warnings in three months; 106 (42%) were accepted directly, leaving 58% needing custom/equivalent fixes, code removal, assertion or another pattern.
independent_evidence.strength: Peer-reviewed production integration; narrow learned repair patterns, not general coding agents.

production_activity: 659 Devin PRs merged in one week at Cognition (first-party, 2026), versus its best 2025 week of 154.
Cognition productivity-estimator dataset: 258 sessions, 126 users, eight deployments; approximately 1-20% of non-PR sessions classified unproductive depending on customer.

Rakuten: claimed feature cycle 24 to 5 working days (79%); claimed 99.9% accuracy on complex code modifications; one seven-hour autonomous run in 12.5M-line codebase. Definitions and denominators are not published.

TELUS: claimed 57,000 active generative-AI users, 500,000+ hours saved, $90M+ benefit across 47 large-scale solutions and 30% faster engineering shipping. Attribution to Claude/coding agents and cost basis are not isolated.
Cognition 2025 aggregate: vendor-reported 67% of Devin PRs merged versus 34% in the prior year; merge does not measure latent defects or reviewer cost.
OpenAI 2025 internal rollout: nearly all engineers reportedly used Codex and merged 70% more PRs/week; uncontrolled before/after correlation with no task-size or defect adjustment.
Wiz migration: claimed 50,000 Python lines to 18,413 Go lines in about 20 hours versus a 2-3 specialist-month estimate; 99% differential parity still hid 20-30 distinct issues.
Money Forward: >80% adoption, >90% code acceptance, and early-adopter self-report of seven hours saved/engineer/week; selection, task counts and defect rates unknown.
controlled_or_independent: METR early 2025: 19% slower across 246 issues/16 maintainers.
METR 2026 follow-up: point estimates of 18% and 4% speedup, both statistically compatible with no effect and considered biased.
GitHub 2022 lab task: Copilot group 55% faster (1h11m vs 2h41m) and completion 78% vs 70%; vendor-run, one task, assistant rather than autonomous agent.
GitHub 2024 lab task: 202 valid submissions; access associated with 53.2% greater chance of passing all ten tests and 5% higher blind approval; vendor-run and narrow.
Dependabot 2023 study: >70% of 502,752 PRs merged; median merge lag four hours; 11.3% of projects later deprecated the bot.
Repairnator: only 30.82% of 11,523 CI failures reproduced locally; 0.13% yielded patch candidates; zero passed human overfitting review for submission.
SapFix: 165 generated -> 131 build/test-pass -> 55 shown -> about half judged correct; test pass therefore greatly overstated usable repair.
Getafix: 106/approximately 250 (42%) suggestions accepted with one click; final human disposition remained necessary.
cost_and_burden: GitHub cloud-agent sessions consume both Actions minutes and AI credits; current individual sticker prices shown on the accessed plan page are $10/$39/$100 per user-month with included credits. Actual run cost varies by model/tokens and CI time.
Cognition's estimator is noisy per session: about 50% within factor two and 2-3x errors common; therefore ROI measurement itself needs aggregation and maintenance.

Unpriced but repeatedly observed costs: repository setup/indexing, custom instructions/playbooks, MCP credentials, CI compute, flaky-test handling, human clarification/review, failed-session triage, post-merge defect remediation and security governance.
No cited vendor case provides a complete total-cost-of-ownership calculation or controlled net ROI after those costs.

reference_workflow.mechanics: Accept only authenticated triggers from an issue tracker, dependency alert, scheduled audit, CI/observability event or approved chat user. Store task ID, repository, requester, risk class, acceptance tests and budget. Reject vague or impossible requests to clarification rather than letting the agent persist.

A deterministic controller checks repo ownership, single/multi-repo need, data sensitivity, deploy impact and available verification. Route low-risk lockfile/docs/lint/test work to automation; route product ambiguity, migrations and security-critical work to a human planner.

Index only needed code/docs/history. Agent proposes affected files, tests, external tools, stop conditions and rollback. Human approves plans for schema/API/auth/infrastructure changes. Split long work into isolated sessions; GitHub's cloud agent has a 59-minute hard cap.

Create ephemeral least-privilege workspace and dedicated branch. Default network deny/allowlist. Provide short-lived secrets only when required. External production systems and databases are read-only. Record prompts, commands, tool calls, token/CI usage and artifacts.

Run formatting, lint, unit/integration/contract/property/security/license checks. Reproduce bugs first and add regression tests. Treat agent self-review as advisory; use an independent reviewer/tool and verify generated tests are meaningful.

Open one small PR with task link, plan, diff summary, tests, unresolved risks, generated-code disclosure, cost and rollback. Failed checks trigger a bounded repair loop; repeated or novel failure escalates with full trace.

Branch protection, CODEOWNERS and required checks remain authoritative. Allow bot automerge only for preclassified reversible changes with strong tests (for example lockfile maintenance or known-safe patch updates). Agent PRs that affect behavior require human approval.

Normal signed CI/CD deploys, not the coding agent. Use canary/feature flag, health/SLO and security checks, automatic rollback and incident escalation. No agent receives direct unrestricted production write access.

Link incidents, rollbacks, review edits and escaped defects to session/task. Measure accepted/merged/reverted rates, lead and review time, human touches, compute/credit cost, change failure rate and net hours. Promote a task class to more autonomy only after enough local evidence; version playbooks and policies.

execution: GitHub Actions or equivalent ephemeral runners
control_and_output: protected branches, CODEOWNERS, merge queues and required checks
PR with audit trace and cost metadata
signed CI/CD, feature flags, canary, SLO alarms and rollback

human_gates.why: Operational failures often begin with impossible or underspecified tasks; Answer.AI observed days of futile work.
Humans own product intent, architecture, cross-repository coordination, schema/API/auth/infrastructure and legal/security decisions.
Prompt injection or compromised repository content can turn agent tool access into data exfiltration or supply-chain action.
GitHub's default design requires a write-user to approve workflow execution and preserves required approvals; agent self-review is not independent assurance.
Delivery stability can worsen even when local coding metrics improve; deployment uses the existing accountable release process.
Timeout, repeated failed tests, ambiguous expected behavior, unexpected diff size, missing credentials, security findings or budget breach must stop rather than invite unbounded retries.

modes: tests generated to match the bug rather than intent
passing narrow unit tests while breaking contracts/performance/security
merged PR used as a false proxy for value or quality
99% differential parity can still conceal dozens of edge-case defects, as Wiz's customer story reports
CI failure cannot be reproduced locally because environment/flakiness differs
patch passes the failing test but overfits and is not semantically correct
branch drift/rebase churn and merge-queue serialization
repair suggestions spam maintainers; SapFix stopped a high-volume experiment after three days
self-selection and survivor bias in case studies
parallel sessions make time accounting hard
license plus compute plus review exceeds saved labor
junior skill erosion or reviewers rubber-stamp
fast output expands batch size and harms stability

controls_and_mitigations: Use a risk-tier allowlist: deterministic dependency/docs/test chores first; never grant blanket autonomy by repository.
Keep agents on ephemeral branches/runners with least privilege, egress allowlists, short-lived secrets, read-only production observability/data and explicit tool schemas.
Preserve protected branches, CODEOWNERS, required CI/security checks, merge queues and signed releases. Do not let the same agent author, approve and deploy.
Set hard limits for time, tokens/credits, commands, retries, diff size, files/repositories and concurrent sessions. Escalate on limit rather than silently extend.
Require bug reproduction and regression tests; add contract/integration/property/fuzz/security/performance tests according to risk. Mutate or inspect generated tests to avoid tautological checks.

For dependencies, use cooldown/minimum release age where supported, group carefully, pin digests/lockfiles, produce SBOMs, and automerge only after meaningful checks. Keep majors and production-critical libraries human-reviewed.
Canary/feature-flag behavioral changes, watch SLOs and business metrics, auto-rollback, and link incident/revert data to the originating agent session.
Maintain versioned custom instructions/playbooks with postconditions and forbidden actions. Treat repository text, issue text and web pages as untrusted input.

Audit outcomes by cohort and task class: assignment-to-accepted PR, merge and revert rates, escaped defects, review minutes, total cost, lead time and change failure rate. Run holdouts where feasible.

For migrations, run old and new implementations in parallel behind a feature flag and compare outputs on real traffic; investigate the residual mismatches rather than accepting a high aggregate parity percentage.

Measure repair as a full funnel (trigger → reproduced → compiled → tests passed → reviewer-accepted → merged → no regression). A test-passing patch is only a candidate; retain semantic/human review and suppress duplicate/noisy proposals.

maturity_assessment.rating: Conditionally useful in production; mature for narrow deterministic maintenance; emerging for general issue-to-PR; not production-ready for unattended end-to-end project ownership.
maturity_assessment.rationale: Existence and volume are proven, but general success-rate evidence is sparse and inconsistent. Strong outcomes cluster around scoped, well-tested, reversible tasks with good repository context. Real deployments shift labor from typing to specification, environment setup, review and governance. Independent trials and surveys show large failure, distrust and debugging burdens.

build_vs_buy.buy: Hosted agents (GitHub Copilot cloud agent, Devin, Claude Code) buy sandbox execution, models, repository UI/integrations and upgrades. Dependabot buys GitHub-native dependency alerts/PRs. This reduces platform work but creates metered usage, data/control-plane and vendor-lock-in concerns.
build_vs_buy.build_or_self_host: Renovate/self-hosted runners or custom orchestration give policy, network, model and data control. They require queue/state/idempotency, workspace lifecycle, secret brokerage, logging, upgrades, evals and on-call ownership.
build_vs_buy.always_custom: Repository instructions, executable acceptance tests, risk classification, identity/permission mapping, MCP/tool allowlists, CI gates, release/canary/rollback, cost attribution and outcome dashboards are organization-specific even when the agent is bought.
build_vs_buy.decision_rule: Buy agent execution first; build the thin policy/evidence control plane around it. Self-host only for regulated data, bespoke tools, predictable high volume or vendor-independent operation where a team can own the maintenance burden.

recommended_pattern.implementation: Start with a shadow lane for dependency, documentation, test, lint and reproducible small-bug tasks. The agent may research, plan, edit and open a PR, but cannot approve or deploy. After a local sample (for example 50-100 tasks per task class) meets preset accepted-PR, escaped-defect, review-time and net-cost thresholds, permit CI-gated automerge only for the lowest-risk reversible class. Keep behavioral changes human reviewed and production rollout under ordinary CI/CD.
recommended_pattern.operating_model: One durable controller owns intake, state, budgets, retries and audit. Use disposable execution workers. Separate author/reviewer/deployer identities. Version task policies and playbooks. Feed review edits, failed CI, rollbacks and incidents into an eval set before changing prompts/models or expanding autonomy.
recommended_pattern.success_criteria: Report accepted/merged/reverted/incident rates rather than raw PRs or tokens; median/p95 lead and human-review time; cost per accepted change including CI and review; change failure/SLO impact; and task-class coverage. Maintain a non-agent or prior-version control cohort where practical.
recommended_pattern.do_not_do: Do not infer production reliability from SWE-bench alone, use merged PRs as the only success label, expose broad production credentials, disable approvals to increase throughput, or scale parallel agents faster than review and deployment capacity.

open_questions: What are audited task-level success, revert and escaped-defect rates for current 2026 versions across representative enterprise repositories?
What is net TCO after subscriptions/API tokens, Actions/runner compute, integration upkeep, reviewer time, failed attempts and incident remediation?
Which task features predict success well enough for safe automatic routing, and how stable are those predictors across model upgrades?
Do gains persist under randomized organization-level measurement when workers can use multiple concurrent agents without selection bias?
How often do agent-authored changes cause delayed security/reliability regressions after merge, and who bears liability?
What is the right independent-review design when both author and reviewer use correlated models/training data?
How can multi-repository and long-running tasks preserve state, least privilege and rollback without widening blast radius?
How much ongoing labor do repository instructions, playbooks, MCP integrations and eval suites require per month?

confidence.reason: The source set deliberately triangulates product docs, first-party production use, vendor customer stories, practitioner failures, randomized trials and broad surveys. However, standardized audited production success/TCO data remain rare and fast model/product changes reduce temporal transfer.

conflicts.claims: Selected enterprise/customer stories report 30-79% faster delivery and large savings, while Answer.AI saw only 3/20 successes and METR early-2025 found 19% slowdown.
conflicts.likely_explanation: Different product generations, task selection, repository familiarity, training/support, success definitions and publication/selection bias. Customer stories omit failed-task denominators; METR covers experienced maintainers and bounded real issues.

conflicts.claims: GitHub lab experiments show 55% faster completion and quality gains, while DORA associates greater AI use with reduced throughput/stability.
conflicts.likely_explanation: A single-task individual coding measure is not system delivery performance. Faster code can increase batch size/review/deployment load; observational DORA results are also not causal.

conflicts.claims: METR early-2025 found slowdown; raw late-2025/early-2026 follow-up suggests 4-18% speedup; 2026 survey reports 1.4-2x value and 3x speed.
conflicts.likely_explanation: Tools improved, but later experiment suffered strong opt-out/task-selection and concurrent-agent measurement bias; surveys overstate counterfactual time (40 percentage points in METR's prior comparison). Treat direction as plausible, magnitude unknown.

conflicts.claims: High adoption coexists with low trust and non-mainstream agent use.
conflicts.likely_explanation: Developers use AI selectively as an assistant while retaining review; usage is not evidence of unattended autonomy or positive net ROI.

conflicts.claims: Cognition reports 67% PR merge rate and OpenAI reports 70% more PRs/week, but neither establishes equivalent useful or reliable output.
